+# ADR 0001: Raise Pricing Cache TTL
+
+**Status:** Accepted
+
+## Context
+
+The pricing API responses are cached to reduce redundant requests and improve performance across the system. The cache TTL (time-to-live) has historically been set to 900 seconds (15 minutes), which was a conservative default chosen when cache infrastructure and monitoring were less mature. Over time, pricing data has become more stable in production, with fewer than anticipated dynamic changes requiring immediate invalidation. Monitoring shows that cache misses due to TTL expiry account for a significant portion of API traffic during peak periods, and pricing data consistency is maintained through separate invalidation channels when changes do occur.
+
+Extending the TTL reduces load on the pricing API, improves response times for repeat queries, and lowers operational costs associated with cache misses and backend requests. The trade-off is accepting slightly stale pricing data for most consumers, but this aligns with current product requirements where near-real-time pricing is not critical.
+
+## Decision
+
+We will raise the pricing cache TTL from 900 seconds to 3600 seconds (1 hour). This change applies to all pricing API responses cached at the application level. Cache invalidation via explicit cache purge remains the primary mechanism for reflecting urgent pricing changes, and should continue to be triggered by pricing updates in the database.
+
+## Consequences
+
+The reduction in cache misses is expected to decrease pricing API query volume by approximately 60%, translating to meaningful cost savings and reduced tail latency during traffic spikes. Most clients will see improved response times and reduced dependency on backend systems. Pricing data will be stale for up to one hour for consumers who receive cached responses; this is acceptable for the current use cases, though any future features requiring real-time pricing should reconsider this TTL or implement more granular caching strategies.
+
+We should monitor cache hit rates, API latency, and client-side pricing staleness after the rollout to verify the expected benefits. If unexpected issues arise (such as customer complaints about stale pricing), we can adjust the TTL back to a lower value or implement conditional cache invalidation tied to pricing change frequency.
